newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares recover as Wall Street ticks up.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares recover as Wall Street ticks up.

text.p: Italian shares recovered from early losses to close slightly higher on Tuesday helped by the early firmer trend on Wall Street and the strength of some individual shares such as ENI and Benetton, dealers said.

Stocks had started lower in a market that lacked real direction and drifted down in line with domestic bonds, but ENI continued to shine and ended up 1.33 percent at 7,445 lire after the Treasury announced Monday that the second tranche of shares to be floated would be less than the market had expected.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 0.09 percent at 9,999 and Mib30 index 0.2 percent firmer at 15,049.

Dealers said shares in clothing group Benetton firmed to close up 3.19 percent at 17,615 lire after some analysts turned positive on the stock following a meeting with the company on Friday which followed the group's first-half 1996 results.

Analysts said that there was a strong positive message from Benetton's management and after the shares had underperformed over the last few weeks some analysts said it was time to move to a buy stance.
Telecom stocks were out of favour ahead of the flotation of Deutsche Telekom. STET slipped 0.31 percent to 5,213 lire, while TIM and Telecom Italia showed only marginal gains.
Fiat hit a new low dropping to 4,085 lire the lowest level seen since January 1994. The shares suffering from the poor Italian car market and a high lira closed down 1.53 percent at 4,109 lire.
